answer: Yes. The subtext enriches the story rather than feeling forced. Quentin’s corporate euphemisms conceal shame and a fear of appearing imperfect, while his handling of the two cups quietly exposes the vulnerability his polished language tries to hide. The woman’s restrained responses suggest both frustration and continued care. Set against the ordinary municipal pool, these tensions make Quentin’s loss of composure especially revealing. Although the narrator later explains much of their significance, the dialogue and gestures establish these meanings convincingly first.
